text: Which of the following predicate logic formulae is/are CORRECT representation(s) of the statement: "Everyone has exactly one mother"? The meanings of the predicates used are: mother(y, x): y is the mother of x; noteq(x, y): x and y are not equal.
options: (for all x)(there exists y)(there exists z)(mother(y, x) and not mother(z, x))
(for all x)(there exists y)[mother(y, x) and (for all z)(noteq(z, y) implies not mother(z, x))]
(for all x)(for all y)[mother(y, x) implies (there exists z)(mother(z, x) and not noteq(z, y))]
(for all x)(there exists y)[mother(y, x) and not (there exists z)(noteq(z, y) and mother(z, x))]
solution: (B) and (D) say the same thing: there is a mother y of x, and any z that is a mother of x is not different from y, that is z = y. (A) merely asserts that some y is a mother and some z is not, which holds in almost any class and says nothing about uniqueness. (C) demands, for every mother y of x, a further mother z different from y, which forces at least two mothers.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page for GATE CS 2025 Set 1 Q.38 with the accepted answer
answer_evidence: The accepted answer states 'B & D matches', after rewriting (B) into the equivalent form of (D).
